newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia rights workers find another dead royalist.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia rights workers find another dead royalist.

text.p: Human rights investigators in Cambodia on Thursday found the body of a royalist soldier apparently murdered while in the custody of forces loyal to strongman Hun Sen.

The body of the man, who had been strangled, was found some 100 meters (yards) from an army camp that had been used as a detention centre for royalist troops after the bloody July 6 ouster of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

A United Nations human rights official said his office was alerted to the case after witnesses said they had seen the man, one of Ranariddh's bodyguards, beaten by soldiers at a detention camp on the outskirts of Phnom Penh.

Hundreds of soldiers and officials loyal to Ranariddh were rounded up in the aftermath of his overthrow by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and rights workers and diplomatic sources say at least 40 of them were subsequently killed.
"We came here, we found a fresh grave, we have dug up the grave and found this person," Balaskrishnan Rajagopal of the United Nations Centre for Human Rights in Cambodia told Reuters at the scene.
"We found a rope around his neck...this is a clear case of death by strangulation," he said.
"As to why -- we don't know," he said.
Rajagopal said his office would inform the government of the discovery.
Last week U.N. rights workers found the decomposing bodies of two executed men they feared had been Ranariddh loyalists.
The two bodies were buried in shallow graves, in a gully off a main road 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Phnom Penh. They had been bound, blindfolded and shot.
Hun Sen's government has said one senior royalist official was executed after his arrest. Several other senior FUNCINPEC officials are known to have been killed.

Hun Sen has denied human rights abuses and has invited rights groups to investigate the situation in the country. He also said members of parliament from all parties would probe reports of rights abuses.
